1.note: Jeremiah is using the words translated as **Now it happened in that year** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.

1.q: בְּ⁠רֵאשִׁית֙ מַמְלֶ֨כֶת֙ צִדְקִיָּ֣ה מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה ב⁠שנת הָֽ⁠רְבִעִ֔ית בַּ⁠חֹ֖דֶשׁ הַ⁠חֲמִישִׁ֑י
1.note: Here Jeremiah is providing background information to help readers understand what happens next in the story. In your translation, introduce this information in a way that would be natural in your own language and culture.
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **reign**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the time when Zedekiah ruled as]

1.q: חֲנַנְיָה֩ בֶן עַזּ֨וּר הַ⁠נָּבִ֜יא אֲשֶׁ֤ר מִ⁠גִּבְעוֹן֙
1.note: Here Jeremiah is introducing **Hananiah** as a new participant in the story. Your language may have its own way of introducing new participants that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [a certain man named Hananiah, the son of Azzur, a prophet from Gibeon]
The word **Azzur** is the name of a man.

Jeremiah is using **to the eyes of** as a common expression of the culture to mean “in the presence of.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. This also occurs in verses 5 and 11. Alternate translation: [in the sight of the priests and all the people]

Jeremiah is using the word **saying** to indicate that what follows is a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of indicating direct quotations in your language. This also occurs in verses 2 and 11–13.

If your language would not represent a number in a form such as **fourth** or **fifth**, you could represent this number in a form that your language would use. Alternate translation: [in month five of year four]

2.q: כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵ⁠אמֹ֑ר שָׁבַ֞רְתִּי אֶת עֹ֖ל מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶֽל
2.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says that he has broken the yoke of the king of Babylon]

Here Hananiah is speaking as if the control that the king of Babylon has over other nations were a **yoke** that could be broken. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. This also occurs in verse 4. Alternate translation: [the power of the king of Babylon over the nations]
See how you translated the similar expression in 6:6. This also occurs in verses 11, 13, 14, and 16.

3.q: בְּ⁠ע֣וֹד שְׁנָתַ֣יִם יָמִ֗ים אֲנִ֤י מֵשִׁיב֙ אֶל הַ⁠מָּק֣וֹם הַ⁠זֶּ֔ה אֶֽת כָּל כְּלֵ֖י בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר לָקַ֜ח נְבוּכַדנֶאצַּ֤ר מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶל֙ מִן הַ⁠מָּק֣וֹם הַ⁠זֶּ֔ה וַ⁠יְבִיאֵ֖⁠ם בָּבֶֽל
3.note: The phrase **Within two years of days** shows that this event will not happen right away but at a later time. Your language may have a connecting phrase that you can use to show this. Alternate translation: [Two full years from now, I, myself, will bring back to this place all the vessels of the house of Yahweh that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took from this place and brought them to Babylon]

Hananiah is using **two years of days** as a common expression of the culture to mean “two full years.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. This also occurs in verse 11. Alternate translation: [two complete years]

The pronoun **I** refers to Yahweh, whom Hananiah claims to be quoting, and not to Hananiah himself. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [I, Yahweh, myself, am bringing back]

4.note: The word translated as **for** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [because]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **exile**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [all the people of Judah who were taken away captive]

Here, **exile**, although singular in form, represents the people who were carried away into exile. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [all the people of Judah who were carried away]
See how you translated **the declaration of Yahweh** in 1:8.

5.q: וַ⁠יֹּ֨אמֶר֙ יִרְמְיָ֣ה הַ⁠נָּבִ֔יא אֶל חֲנַנְיָ֖ה הַ⁠נָּבִ֑יא
5.note: Jeremiah is using the phrase **And Jeremiah the prophet said to Hananiah the prophet** to indicate that what follows is a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of indicating direct quotations in your language. This also occurs in verse 15.

6.q: וַ⁠יֹּ֨אמֶר֙ יִרְמְיָ֣ה הַ⁠נָּבִ֔יא אָמֵ֕ן כֵּ֖ן יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה יְהוָ֑ה יָקֵ֤ם יְהוָה֙ אֶת דְּבָרֶ֔י⁠ךָ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִבֵּ֗אתָ לְ⁠הָשִׁ֞יב כְּלֵ֤י בֵית יְהוָה֙ וְ⁠כָל הַ⁠גּוֹלָ֔ה מִ⁠בָּבֶ֖ל אֶל הַ⁠מָּק֥וֹם הַ⁠זֶּֽה
6.note: Here, **to** marks **to bring back the vessels of the house of Yahweh and all the exiles from Babylon to this place** as the goal or purpose of **May Yahweh establish your words that you prophesied**. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose.

The word **Amen** is a Hebrew word. You will need to decide if you will use this word in its Hebrew form or if you will instead translate the meaning into your language. Either approach has broad support. If you use the Hebrew word, you could spell it the way it sounds in your language and then put the translation in a footnote. Alternate translation: [So be it]

6.q: כֵּ֖ן יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה יְהוָ֑ה יָקֵ֤ם יְהוָה֙ אֶת־דְּבָרֶ֔י⁠ךָ
6.note: Jeremiah is saying what he wants Yahweh to do. See the discussion in the introduction to this book about “let” and “may” and follow the decision of your team of how a speaker will express in this context what he wants someone to do. Alternate translation: [I desire that Yahweh do this! I desire that Yahweh establish your words]

7.q: אַךְ שְׁמַֽע נָא֙ הַ⁠דָּבָ֣ר הַ⁠זֶּ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָנֹכִ֖י דֹּבֵ֣ר בְּ⁠אָזְנֶ֑י⁠ךָ וּ⁠בְ⁠אָזְנֵ֖י כָּל הָ⁠עָֽם
7.note: Jeremiah uses the word **But** here to indicate a contrast between his wish that Hananiah’s words would come true and the warning that he is about to give. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Even so, please hear this word that I myself am speaking in your ears and in the ears of all the people]
The pronoun **I** refers to Jeremiah himself, not to Yahweh. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [this word that I, Jeremiah, am indeed speaking]

Jeremiah is using **in your ears and in the ears of all the people** as a common expression of the culture to mean “where you and all the people can hear it.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [where you and all the people can hear it]

8.q: הַ⁠נְּבִיאִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָי֧וּ לְ⁠פָנַ֛⁠י וּ⁠לְ⁠פָנֶ֖י⁠ךָ מִן הָֽ⁠עוֹלָ֑ם
8.note: Jeremiah is using **The prophets who were to the face of me and to the face of you from ancient time** to describe something that was ongoing. This provides the background for other events he will describe that began to happen during this time. Connect this clause to the story in a way that makes it clear in your language that this clause is describing something that was ongoing in the background. Alternate translation: [From ancient times, long before you and I lived, there were prophets]

Jeremiah is using the expression **to the face of me and to the face of you** to mean “before” or “previous to.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [before me and you]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **war**, **disaster**, and **plague**, you could express the same ideas in another way. Alternate translation: [saying that armies would attack them, that they would suffer terribly, and that they would become deathly sick]

9.q: הַ⁠נָּבִ֕יא אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִנָּבֵ֖א לְ⁠שָׁל֑וֹם בְּ⁠בֹא֙ דְּבַ֣ר הַ⁠נָּבִ֗יא יִוָּדַע֙ הַ⁠נָּבִ֔יא
9.note: Jeremiah is presenting a possible condition, that people will recognize a prophet who prophesies peace as one whom Yahweh has truly sent only if what that prophet says actually happens. Use a natural form in your language for introducing a condition that could happen. It may be helpful to reorder this sentence so that the conditional statement is first. Alternate translation: [If a prophet prophesies of peace and then the word of that prophet comes true, that prophet will be known]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **peace**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [that things will be peaceful]

The expression **will be known** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [people will know that prophet]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **truth**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [as his genuine messenger]
See how you translated the similar expression in 23:16.

10.q: וַ⁠יִּקַּ֞ח חֲנַנְיָ֤ה הַ⁠נָּבִיא֙ אֶת הַ⁠מּוֹטָ֔ה מֵ⁠עַ֕ל צַוַּ֖אר יִרְמְיָ֣ה הַ⁠נָּבִ֑יא וַֽ⁠יִּשְׁבְּרֵֽ⁠הוּ
10.note: Taking the yoke bar off Jeremiah’s neck and breaking it was a symbolic action by which Hananiah showed that he believed Yahweh would soon end the rule of the king of Babylon over the nations. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [And Hananiah the prophet, to show that he believed Yahweh would soon end the rule of the king of Babylon over the nations, took the yoke bar from upon the neck of Jeremiah the prophet and broke it]

11.q: כֹּה֮ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָה֒ כָּ֣כָה אֶשְׁבֹּ֞ר אֶת עֹ֣ל נְבֻֽכַדְנֶאצַּ֣ר
11.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [saying that Yahweh says that, in the same way, he will break the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar]

11.q: אֶת־עֹ֣ל נְבֻֽכַדְנֶאצַּ֣ר מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֗ל בְּ⁠עוֹד֙ שְׁנָתַ֣יִם יָמִ֔ים מֵ⁠עַ֕ל צַוַּ֖אר כָּל־הַ⁠גּוֹיִ֑ם
11.note: Here Hananiah is speaking as if the control that Nebuchadnezzar has over other nations were a **yoke** resting on their **neck**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the power of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon within two more years of days from over all the nations]

Jeremiah is using **went on his way** as a common expression of the culture to mean “departed.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And Jeremiah the prophet departed]

12.note: Jeremiah is using the words translated as **And the word of Yahweh was** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.

12.q: וַ⁠יְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֶֽל־יִרְמְיָ֑ה אַ֠חֲרֵי שְׁב֞וֹר חֲנַנְיָ֤ה הַ⁠נָּבִיא֙ אֶת־הַ⁠מּוֹטָ֔ה
12.note: The word **after** shows the sequence of these events: Hananiah broke the yoke bar first, and then Yahweh spoke to Jeremiah. Your language may have a connecting phrase that you can use to show this. Alternate translation: [once Hananiah the prophet had broken the yoke bar from upon the neck of Jeremiah the prophet]
See how you translated the similar expression in 8:9.

13.q: הָלוֹךְ֩ וְ⁠אָמַרְתָּ֨ אֶל חֲנַנְיָ֜ה לֵ⁠אמֹ֗ר כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה מוֹטֹ֥ת עֵ֖ץ שָׁבָ֑רְתָּ וְ⁠עָשִׂ֥יתָ תַחְתֵּי⁠הֶ֖ן מֹט֥וֹת בַּרְזֶֽל
13.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Go, and you shall tell Hananiah that Yahweh says that he has broken yoke bars of wood, but that he will make in their place yoke bars of iron]

Yahweh uses the word **but** here to indicate a contrast between the wooden yoke bars that Hananiah broke and the iron yoke bars that will take their place. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [however, in their place you will make]

13.q: מוֹטֹ֥ת עֵ֖ץ שָׁבָ֑רְתָּ וְ⁠עָשִׂ֥יתָ תַחְתֵּי⁠הֶ֖ן מֹט֥וֹת בַּרְזֶֽל
13.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if the rule that the king of Babylon has over the nations were **yoke bars of wood** that Hananiah had broken and that Yahweh would replace with much stronger **yoke bars of iron**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [You have broken the current weak rule of Babylon over the nations, but soon Babylon will rule over them so strongly that no one will be able to break that yoke]

14.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 6:6.

14.q: כִּ֣י כֹֽה אָמַר֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל עֹ֣ל בַּרְזֶ֡ל נָתַ֜תִּי
14.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [For Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says that he has put a yoke of iron]

14.q: עֹ֣ל בַּרְזֶ֡ל נָתַ֜תִּי עַל־צַוַּ֣אר כָּל־הַ⁠גּוֹיִ֣ם הָ⁠אֵ֗לֶּה
14.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if the rule that he has given Nebuchadnezzar over these nations were **a yoke of iron** that he had placed on their **neck**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I have placed all these nations under an unbreakable obligation]

Here, **to** marks **to serve Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon** as the goal or purpose of **I have put a yoke of iron on the neck of all these nations**. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose. Alternate translation: [that they should serve Nebuchadnezzar]

Yahweh is using **the beast of the field** as a common expression of the culture to mean “the animals that live in open country.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the animals that live in open country]
See how you translated the similar expression in 27:6.
In this verse, the word **animal** is singular in form, but it refers to all wild animals as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural form of “animal” as in the UST.

15.q: וְ⁠אַתָּ֗ה הִבְטַ֛חְתָּ אֶת הָ⁠עָ֥ם הַ⁠זֶּ֖ה עַל שָֽׁקֶר
15.note: Jeremiah is using the emphatic pronoun **you yourself** to contrast what Hananiah has done with what Yahweh has not done. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and it is you who have made this people trust in falsehood]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **falsehood**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [in what is false]

16.note: The term translated as **Therefore** indicates that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes this clear. Alternate translation: [For this reason]
See how you translated the similar expression in 2:5.

Yahweh is referring to causing Hananiah to die in a polite way by using the phrase **I am sending you away from upon the face of the earth**. Depending on what is helpful for your readers, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [Behold, I am about to cause you to die]

Yahweh is using **Behold me** as an expression that people of this culture would commonly use to mean that they were about to do something. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Now I am about to send you away]
See how you translated this expression in 25:26.

The word translated as **for** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [Since]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **rebellion**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [rebellious things]

17.q: וַ⁠יָּ֛מָת חֲנַנְיָ֥ה הַ⁠נָּבִ֖יא בַּ⁠שָּׁנָ֣ה הַ⁠הִ֑יא בַּ⁠חֹ֖דֶשׁ הַ⁠שְּׁבִיעִֽי
17.note: **And Hananiah the prophet died in that year, in the seventh month** is a comment about what happened after the story as a result of the events within the story itself. This signals the end of a story. Use the natural form in your language for expressing the conclusion of a story. Alternate translation: [So it happened that Hananiah the prophet died that very year, in month seven]
